question: Which statement best describes What decorators are?
options: A decorator is a function applied with @ syntax to a declaration. The compiler calls it with information about the thing it decorates, letting the decorator observe, modify, or replace it. Decorators are a declarative way to attach cross-cutting behavior (logging, validation, dependency injection) without cluttering the decorated code.

Property decorators run on a field declaration and are typically used to record metadata (e.g. validation rules) rather than alter behavior directly. Parameter decorators receive the position of a constructor or method parameter and are central to dependency injection, marking which dependency to inject.

A class decorator receives the class constructor and can inspect it, replace it, or attach metadata. Frameworks use class decorators like @Component or @Injectable to register a class and configure it. Returning a new constructor lets a decorator extend or wrap the class.

A method decorator receives the target, the method name, and (in legacy mode) the property descriptor, so it can wrap or replace the method — e.g. to add logging, timing, or memoization. Accessor decorators work the same way for getters/setters.
